summary: Well‑executed, preregistered paired emulation study that ran exactly as specified and archived extensive artifacts. The preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics produced identical initial model outputs for both arms, so no validator‑triggered repairs occurred and the paired contrast is degenerate (n10 = n01 = 0). Main scientific record and execution/accounting are transparent and reproducible. The manuscript must correct bibliographic/citation formatting to a conventional IEEE numbered bibliography and verify citation support in‑text before finalisation.
critical_issues: References are not provided in a conventional IEEE numbered bibliography with full bibliographic metadata; cited_record_ids currently appear as raw URLs/identifiers. This violates the venue requirement that prose use IEEE numbered markers and that each cited record actually support the proximate claim. This is a mandatory formatting and citation‑integrity defect that must be fixed prior to finalisation.
required_revisions: Convert the References section into a conventional IEEE numbered bibliography (authors, title, venue, year, DOI/arXiv as appropriate) and ensure all in‑text citations use corresponding IEEE numeric markers. Verify and, if necessary, correct each citation so the cited record supports the specific claim in the nearby sentence (do not leave raw DOI/arXiv/identifier entries in the prose or reference list).

Explicitly confirm in Methods (not only in Discussion) that shared_initial_candidate semantics produced a single initial LLM generation per task reused across paired arms, and add a single clear sentence stating the consequence: the paired contrast only tests validator/repair effects conditional on initial candidates failing validation (i.e., generator variability between arms was intentionally constrained). This sentence may be brief because the run artifacts already reflect this, but it must be present in Methods for clarity and preregistration fidelity.
optional_revisions: Add a brief table or footnote mapping the numbered IEEE references to the archived record identifiers/hashes in the evidence bundle to aid reviewers/readers who wish to cross‑check the primary sources.

Expand the Discussion slightly to give more detail about the task generator’s role (why baseline unsafe rate was zero) and about the verifier rule coverage (examples of rule classes covered vs uncovered) to contextualize the null result for practitioners.

Include a short explicit recommendation checklist for follow‑up runs (e.g., independent initial-generation contrast, larger repair budgets, stronger/adaptive adversary procedures) as a compact actionable item list.
